title: Algebraic proof
examples: How do I prove that the product of two consecutive even numbers is always divisible by 8?
Can you show me how to prove that the sum of any odd number and the next even number is always odd?

explain.say: Today we will learn to prove things using algebra. We will look at even and odd numbers first.
An even number can always be written as two times some whole number. We call this two n. For example, eight is two times four.
An odd number is always one more than an even number. So we write it as two n plus one. For example, eleven is two times five plus one.
Next we look at consecutive integers. These are numbers right next to each other. We can represent them as n, n plus one, and n plus two.
Let us prove the sum of three consecutive integers is a multiple of three. The sum is n plus (n plus one) plus (n plus two).

faq.q: What does '2n' mean when I see it in a proof?
faq.a: It means that the number is an even number. The 'n' stands for any whole number you choose.
asks: How do I write any even number using algebra?
What does 2n represent in number theory?

faq.q: If I use 'n' for an integer, can I use it again for something else?
faq.a: You can use the same letter like 'n' as long as you are consistent in your proof. It just represents a variable whole number.
asks: Does 'n' have to be a positive number?
Can I use different letters for different variables?

faq.q: Why do I have to use '2n' for even numbers?
faq.a: Because any even number is perfectly divisible by two. Writing it as two times a number shows that fact.
asks: Is 2n the only way to write an even number?
Why can't I just say '2k' instead?

faq.q: How do I prove that the sum of three consecutive integers is a multiple of three?
faq.a: You write the sum as n plus (n plus one) plus (n plus two). When you simplify that, you get three n plus three, which is three times (n plus one).
asks: Show me the proof for three consecutive numbers.
Is three times (n plus one) always divisible by three?

faq.q: What if the integers are negative numbers?
faq.a: The rules still work for negative numbers. For example, -1, 0, and 1 are consecutive. You can still use the algebraic method.
asks: Does this proof only work for positive numbers?
Can I use negative numbers in my proof?

facts: An even integer can always be expressed in the form two n, where n is an integer.
An odd integer can always be expressed in the form two n plus one, where n is an integer.
Three consecutive integers can be represented algebraically as n, n plus one, and n plus two.
The sum of three consecutive integers is always divisible by three.

quiz.say: If we let the three consecutive integers be n, n+1, and n+2, what is their sum?
quiz.why: Adding n plus n plus n gives three n, and adding 1 plus 2 gives three, so the total is three n plus three.

wrong.0: You only added the three variables together, forgetting the constants.
wrong.1: You incorrectly added the constants, missing the final one.
wrong.3: You forgot to add the extra one and the extra two.

quiz.say: Show that the sum of three consecutive integers is a multiple of three.
quiz.why: The sum simplified to three n plus three, which you can factor as three times the quantity (n plus one).

wrong.0: This incorrectly assumes the largest number is the one that makes the sum a multiple of three.
wrong.2: While this is the correct sum, the question asks to show it is a multiple of three, which requires factoring.
wrong.3: This assumes the middle number is the one being multiplied by three.
